title: HaluEval: A Large-Scale Hallucination Evaluation Benchmark for Large Language Models
abstract: Large language models (LLMs), such as ChatGPT, are prone to generate hallucinations, i.e., content that conflicts with the source or cannot be verified by the factual knowledge. To understand what types of content and to which extent LLMs are apt to hallucinate, we introduce the Hallucination Evaluation for Large Language Models (HaluEval) benchmark, a large collection of generated and human-annotated hallucinated samples for evaluating the performance of LLMs in recognizing hallucination. To generate these samples, we propose a ChatGPT-based two-step framework, i.e., sampling-then-filtering. Besides, we also hire some human labelers to annotate the hallucinations in ChatGPT responses. The empirical results suggest that ChatGPT is likely to generate hallucinated content in specific topics by fabricating unverifiable information (i.e., about 19.5% user queries). Moreover, existing LLMs face great challenges in recognizing the hallucinations in texts. While, our experiments also prove that the hallucination recognition can be improved by providing external knowledge or adding reasoning steps.

claims.text: ChatGPT generates hallucinated content in approximately 19.5% of responses to general user queries.
ChatGPT achieves 62.59% accuracy in recognizing hallucinations in question answering tasks.
ChatGPT achieves 58.53% accuracy in recognizing hallucinations in text summarization tasks.
Providing external knowledge improves ChatGPT's hallucination recognition accuracy in question answering from 62.59% to 76.83%.
Adding chain-of-thought reasoning steps improves ChatGPT's hallucination recognition accuracy in text summarization from 58.53% to 61.21%.
HaluEval benchmark consists of 35,000 total samples comprising 5,000 human-annotated user queries and 30,000 automatically generated task-specific examples.

limitations.text: The quality of generated hallucinated samples is constrained by ChatGPT's capacity to follow complex hallucination sampling instructions.
The benchmark focuses on evaluating LLM hallucination recognition performance but does not investigate underlying causes of hallucination.
Because generated hallucinated samples closely resemble ground-truth text, there is potential risk for misuse.
Prior hallucination work primarily focused on small language models and specific isolated tasks.

future_work.text: Monitor and regulate the spread and usage of the HaluEval benchmark to prevent unexpected misuse.

methodologies.name: Sampling-then-filtering automated hallucination generation
methodologies.description: A two-stage automated generation framework leveraging ChatGPT with one-pass and conversational prompting schemes to sample diverse hallucinated answers followed by ground-truth enhanced filtering to pick hard evaluation candidates.

methodologies.name: User query pre-selection and human annotation
methodologies.description: Selection of 5,000 user queries from Alpaca based on lowest BERTScore similarity across multiple ChatGPT responses, followed by max-voting human annotation for span-level hallucination labeling.
conditions: Max-voting among 3 trained human annotators per sample
